lines: Call notes keep an incident update with the call it belongs to.
Begin by reading the title and call number in Call Details.
This example is Training Only, Responder call and check-in practice, F D fifty-one,
twenty twenty-six, zero zero zero one.
Its Nature describes a fictional industrial alarm exercise.
Check the incident identity before adding information, especially when
several calls have similar names.
Choose Notes to open this call's notes.
The Call Notes panel has a search field, an entry area and Add Note.
In this prepared example, the entry records that a virtual access plan
was reviewed in the Academy software exercise, with no real response
or physical inspection requested.
Use a clear update that distinguishes an observation, a request and completed work.
Review the text before choosing Add Note.
Avoid putting an update on the wrong incident simply because
a notes panel is already open.
Reopen Call Notes and read the saved entry.
The same complete text now appears in the list with Wallace Boden as
its author and a recorded timestamp.
The entry area below is empty again.
Verify the actual saved text as well as its author; a prepared message in an entry
field is different from a listed note.
This gives the next person reviewing the call a specific
update they can find and understand.
On the same call, open the Check-In tab.
This view shows Wallace Boden, the Personnel type, a timer and Check In.
The recorded timer has forty-two minutes and twenty-eight seconds
remaining, with seventeen point five of sixty minutes elapsed.
Read whose timer you are viewing before taking action.
Quick Check-In and Check-In History are also visible.
For this exercise, choose the Check In button on Wallace Boden's card
to review the named confirmation.
The sheet identifies Select Check-In Type, Wallace Boden.
Personnel is selected, and Add Note is optional.
This exercise note explicitly describes a virtual personnel check-in
for Academy software practice.
A software entry should accurately describe what was recorded.
Check the named person, selected type and note, then choose Confirm Check-In once.
Keep actual personnel accountability and any missed check-in response aligned
with your department's procedures.
The returned Personnel card now shows fifty-nine minutes and thirty-eight
seconds remaining and Last check-in, zero point one minutes ago.
Below it, the expanded Check-In History contains a Personnel entry, the same
practice note and its timestamp.
Review the saved history as well as the changed timer.
This recording demonstrates the software check-in; it does not establish physical
arrival or a field safety check.
A visible saved entry is the result to verify before relying on the
software record in a handover.
Community paramedicine and mental health response teams can use clear
updates during coordinated outreach.
Search-and-rescue teams can keep support staff informed, security teams
can document post updates, wildland contractors can coordinate crew
activity, and industrial emergency teams can maintain standby accountability.
Fire and EMS departments can apply the same habits.
Select the intended call, record only what you mean, and inspect the
saved note or check-in history before handing over to another team member.
